pois.name: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
pois.description: Francesco Borromini's 1660 masterpiece (60m spiral lantern). The world's most complex Baroque church plan — a six-pointed star in the courtyard of La Sapienza university.

pois.name: Piazza della Rotonda
pois.description: The square in front of the Pantheon (27 BC/125 AD). The portico columns are monolithic Egyptian granite, each 12m tall. The dome was the largest in the world for 1,300 years.

pois.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
pois.description: Hadrian's mausoleum (135 AD), later the popes' fortress. The terrace (48m) commands the best panorama of the Vatican and the Tiber bend. Tosca ends here.

pois.name: Piazza Navona
pois.description: Built over Domitian's 1st-century stadium. Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers (1651) is flanked by Sant'Agnese — Borromini vs. Bernini at point-blank range.

pois.name: Campo de' Fiori
pois.description: Rome's only piazza without a church — a 14th-century execution square, now an open-air market every morning and Rome's liveliest aperitivo hub at dusk.
